title: Timeline
eyebrow: Lives against the state that governed them
dek: Who this family were living under, and what it did to them. The point is not when people were born — it is what was happening around them when they were.

bands.label: Georgian Britain
bands.note: Robert D'Arcy's whole life, and his son's first thirty-five years. A standing army, a global war every twenty years, and a Board of Ordnance that commissioned engineers without recording where they came from.

bands.label: Convict New South Wales
bands.note: Transportation. It is what brought this family to Australia: not free settlement but a garrison posting aboard a convict ship.

bands.label: Colonial Queensland
bands.note: Separation from New South Wales. A new colony needed a Government Printing Office, a gaol, an electric telegraph and a police force, and this family staffed all four.

bands.label: The Commonwealth
bands.note: Federation, then two wars that took four men out of one family.

events.what: Robert D'Arcy commissioned 2nd Lieutenant, Royal Engineers
Marries Jean Ward at Portsea, 21 June
A son christened at St Michael, Barbados — the Corps posted men across the empire
Constantine D'Arcy dies at Chatham
George Pitt D'Arcy at Orthes, with the 39th Foot
The convict ship England sails: a Major of the 39th, 39 men, 6 women, 7 children, and Mrs D'Arcy in the cabin
Robert D'Arcy dies at Chatham, 13 May. His will is proved 4 July and has never been read
Samuel Charles Sneyd arrives with the 4th (King's Own)
Marries Catherine Margaret Mulcahy at Camden, 13 February
The Chubb capture — a sergeant of the Mounted Police
Major George Pitt D'Arcy dies at Parramatta — “gout which had flown to the head”
Queensland separates from New South Wales. Samuel Sneyd becomes Governor of Brisbane Gaol
William Hartley Sneyd enters the public service, 1 February — the Government Printing Office
Paul Cole Atkinson installs the first organ at All Saints', Wickham Terrace, and plays it
William Hartley Sneyd is insolvent
He is found dead in Victoria Park. His widow's deposition names his father and closes a generation
Three Sneyds and a D'Arcy enlist
Arthur Hartley Sneyd killed at Pozières. Six men give six accounts
Vivian Claude Sneyd wins a Bar to the Military Medal at Westhoek
Lindesay Atkinson D'Arcy dies suddenly at 44, of Botany Street, Clayfield
Kenneth Lindsay D'Arcy's eulogy, delivered in three parts by his three children

close: The bands are the state, not the family. Read the two together and the pattern is hard to miss: this family goes where a government sends it, and gets written down when a government writes it down.
